_comment: BYS360 coverage ratchet baseline. Truthful, re-measured floor for CI's actual test scope (tests/quality -m "ci_safe" -- unchanged literal marker, now naturally selecting 40 more tests via per-file pytestmark -- then tests/integration tests/architecture tests/security tests/critical tests/services tests/migrations tests/workflow tests/release tests/communication tests/behavior tests/mobile + 33 loose tests/test_*.py files, branch=true). This value is NOT aspirational and must NEVER be raised automatically by any script -- raising it is a separate, human-reviewed action after real coverage genuinely improves. See scripts/quality/bys360_coverage_ratchet.py for enforcement logic and its docstring for the no-self-raise constraint.
_history:
BYS360 Final Pre-Live Audit P2-07 (2026-09-28): commands[1] re-synced with the live .github/workflows/bys360-ci.yml, which now also names tests/test_h1e_n_feedback_meeting_p4_archive_status_label_contract.py and tests/test_h1e_n_team_compare_status_label_contract.py (previously never run in CI). Documentation-only: combined_pct/tolerance/test_counts/repeatability are unchanged, no coverage was re-measured; the added scope is a strict superset, so the recorded floor stays a valid lower bound.

BYS360 AE Coverage Metadata Drift Closure (2026-09-02, AA-AH Final Closure Phase 1, HEAD 3681285e6fa0e889bdb53d8de21e366d9a3d42a4): mechanically re-extracted commands[0]/commands[1] above programmatically from the CURRENT .github/workflows/bys360-ci.yml (same scripts/quality/bys360_quality9_ci_gate.workflow_run_commands helper this file has used for every prior commands-field correction, e.g. the 2026-08-11 Metadata Consistency Fix entry below) -- following this file's own established precedent that commands/test_counts/repeatability describe the ACTIVE baseline and must track the live workflow, unlike previous_baseline (which intentionally holds a frozen historical snapshot). The live Step2 command had grown by two tokens since the 2026-08-11 measurement that produced combined_pct=27.62 below: the 'tests/performance' directory and 'tests/test_performance_publish_preflight_rules_behavior.py' (added by the P0 Critical Coverage Hotspot Wave, 2026-08-12, per that wave's own section in tests/architecture/test_ci_coverage_scope_contract.py -- which locked both into the live workflow but never into this file's own commands[1], nor into a re-measured baseline; this closure is documentation-only, not a re-measurement wave). NUMERIC_BASELINE_UNCHANGED: combined_pct/combined_pct_precise/line_pct/branch_pct/lines_covered/lines_valid/branches_covered/branches_valid/tolerance_pct are byte-identical to before this edit -- no coverage was re-run, per this phase's explicit no-re-baseline instruction. Because the live command only ADDS test scope on top of the same pytest/--cov-append invocation (a strict superset, not a divergent one), the existing combined_pct floor remains a valid, if now slightly conservative, lower bound: additional tests can only add covered lines, never remove already-covered ones. test_counts/repeatability were NOT touched here (they describe the actual measured run's collected/passed counts under the OLDER, narrower command, and re-deriving them without a real re-run would itself be a fabrication) -- a human-reviewed re-measurement wave, not this metadata fix, is the correct action if those fields are ever needed to reflect the current live scope. tests/architecture/test_ci_coverage_scope_contract.py gained two new locked assertions (test_tests_performance_directory_is_included_in_coverage_instrumented_ci_step family) so this exact class of commands-field-vs-live-workflow drift is caught immediately and loudly the next time either one changes without the other.

BYS360 Coverage Baseline Metadata Consistency Fix (2026-08-11, follow-up to HEAD b2c687d, not amended): the elevation wave below correctly updated the active combined_pct/lines/branches/measured_at, but left commands/test_counts/repeatability describing the superseded Phase 9 measurement (stale tests/workflow token in commands; test_counts and repeatability still showing Phase 9's 24.16-era numbers) -- a genuine internal-consistency defect in a CURRENT-state artifact, not something that should be historical. Fixed by direct reconstruction, no new coverage measurement wave: commands re-extracted programmatically from the current .github/workflows/bys360-ci.yml (same helper used throughout, scripts/quality/bys360_quality9_ci_gate.workflow_run_commands) -- tests/workflow is gone, the 82-test workflow-cleanup contract is explicitly present in Step2, the 44-test OpenAPI contract is Step1-owned (ci_safe marker, not named in Step2) and therefore correctly absent from the Step2 command string; test_counts rebuilt from real `--collect-only` counts per CI-scoped directory/file (collection only, no coverage re-run) -- step1_ci_safe_passed/step2_broader_scope_passed/total_passed key names preserved exactly (read by tests/architecture/test_ci_coverage_scope_contract.py's existing arithmetic-consistency tests); repeatability updated with the elevation wave's own real 3-independent-run evidence (all 3 runs identical: 27.619308622802812, zero variance) instead of Phase 9's stale figures. previous_baseline is correctly left untouched -- that field's entire purpose is to hold the immediately-preceding (i.e. historical, by design) snapshot, unlike commands/test_counts/repeatability which describe the ACTIVE baseline and must track it. Nothing else changed: combined_pct=27.62, combined_pct_precise=27.619308622802812, tolerance_pct=0.5, and all ratchet methodology (pyproject.toml, .github/workflows/bys360-ci.yml, scripts/quality/bys360_coverage_ratchet.py) remain at 0 diff from the elevation wave.

BYS360 Coverage Baseline Ratchet Elevation (2026-08-11, HEAD 7a03a54effbdfb970b8997f4a5d8f20be4543883): after closing CI_COVERAGE_GATE_DRIFT (the tests/workflow stale CI path that had silently zeroed out Step2's ~3400 tests and this ratchet's own reachability) and wiring the 82-test workflow-cleanup and 44-test OpenAPI-cleanup contracts into real, enforced CI scope, 3 independent fresh measurements were taken: canonical Python 3.12 (C:\bys360\project\.venv, matching this file's environment block exactly), a fresh, unique, worktree-external TEMP/TMP directory per run (per tests/conftest.py's BYS360_PHASE5_PYTEST_TEMP_CONTRACT), and the exact Step1+Step2 pytest commands extracted programmatically from .github/workflows/bys360-ci.yml (never hand-simplified), each invoked as a single unchunked command. All 3 runs produced IDENTICAL aggregate results -- lines 32309/101965, branches 3972/29396, combined_pct_precise=27.619308622802812 every time, zero variance (COVERAGE_STABLE) -- Step1 271 passed/1 skipped/0 failed/0 errors and Step2 3531 passed/2 skipped/0 failed/0 errors in all 3 runs alike. This +3.46-point rise over the prior 24.16 baseline is real test-coverage gain from the CI_COVERAGE_GATE_DRIFT closure restoring ~3400 previously CI-silent tests to actual execution -- not a denominator or scope trick: git diff on pyproject.toml, .github/workflows/bys360-ci.yml, and scripts/quality/bys360_coverage_ratchet.py are all empty for this wave, so [tool.coverage] omit/source/branch=true, --cov=app, and the ratchet's combined-pct formula are byte-identical to the prior baseline's methodology. QUALITY_RATCHET_TIGHTENING, not a gate redefinition. The new baseline is set to the measured value itself (round(27.619308622802812, 2) = 27.62), matching this file's own established Phase 6-9 precedent of recording the true measured floor rather than measured-minus-an-extra-undocumented-margin; tolerance_pct (0.5, unchanged this wave) remains the sole, pre-existing, documented safety margin, giving an effective pass threshold of 27.12%. Verified behaviorally with the real ratchet script: a synthetic measurement at the old 24.16-baseline level now correctly FAILs against the new threshold (it would have PASSed under the old one) -- proven, not assumed, regression protection. TEST_ASSURANCE_PRESERVED: 0 valid node IDs removed, 0 new skip/xfail, CI scope unchanged by this wave. commands/test_counts/repeatability below were left describing the superseded Phase 9 measurement at the time this paragraph was written -- corrected in the follow-up Metadata Consistency Fix entry above (this file's internal consistency, not the ratchet script's behavior, was the gap: the script itself only ever reads combined_pct and tolerance_pct). Previous baseline (Phase 9, 2026-07-27) combined_pct=24.16 -- kept in _history for continuity, not reused as the active floor.

Phase 9 Architecture Marker Hygiene Closure (2026-07-27): tests/architecture/test_survey_live_contract.py's pytest.mark.live/realdb/slow markers (flagged as a Phase 8 follow-up candidate) were confirmed stale by the same criteria as the Phase 8 file: all 3 tests are a static Path.read_text() + string-presence contract check against app/communication/surveys_routes.py, with 0 app.*/DB/network/subprocess/Redis use; the markers predate this repo's earliest visible commit with no recorded rationale, and trace to the exact same baseline-squash commit as the Phase 8 file. Markers removed. Unlike Phase 8, no workflow change was needed: this file already lives in tests/architecture, which the broad coverage-instrumented step already collects as a whole directory with no -m marker filter, so it was already executing in real CI regardless of its (inert, for that step) markers -- confirmed via 2 isolated runs, marker-filtered/unfiltered runs (identical either way), a full-suite-mixed run, and a post-full-suite isolated re-run, all 3/3 passed every time, 0 cross-scope duplicate node IDs. Isolated coverage contribution is 0% (0/101921 lines; pure Path.read_text(), no app.* import) -- unchanged from before, since the file was already running. 2 new contract tests were added to the already-in-scope tests/architecture/test_ci_coverage_scope_contract.py to lock the marker removal in, raising step2_broader_scope_passed by exactly 2 (1585 -> 1587) with 0 coverage impact -- combined coverage measured twice, identically, at 24.16299676341062%, byte-identical to the Phase 8 baseline (confirming 0 measurable coverage change, as expected for 0-import AST contract tests). Previous baseline (Phase 8 Top-Level Test Hygiene Closure, 2026-07-27) was combined_pct=24.16 -- kept in _history for continuity, not reused as the active floor. Earlier baselines: Phase 7 Quality/Top-Level CI Coverage Expansion combined_pct=24.14; Phase 6 Communication/Behavior/Mobile combined_pct=23.45; Critical Operational Expansion combined_pct=23.39; CI Coverage Scope Policy Closure (services-only) combined_pct=23.27; Campaign 1B (2026-07-24) combined_pct=18.85 -- see previous_baseline below for the immediately preceding one.

repeatability.note: 3 independent full runs of the current combined command (both steps), each with a fresh, unique, worktree-external TEMP/TMP directory (canonical Python 3.12), produced an IDENTICAL measurement every time -- zero variance: lines 32309/101965, branches 3972/29396 in all 3 runs. The recorded combined_pct is the true measured value, consistent with lines_covered/lines_valid/branches_covered/branches_valid (see tests/quality/test_bys360_coverage_ratchet.py::test_committed_baseline_counts_are_internally_consistent); the sole safety margin is the pre-existing tolerance_pct field below, unchanged at 0.5 points.

tolerance_rationale: Absorbs float rounding and Windows-worktree-vs-Ubuntu-CI-runner platform noise (this baseline was measured on Windows; the actual CI runner is ubuntu-latest, which can take slightly different code paths on OS-conditional branches). Not intended to absorb a real coverage regression, which is expected to be much larger than 0.5 points in practice.
